title: Desa/kelurahan with theft occurrence during the year preceding Podes May 2024 enumeration
publisher: Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Jawa Barat
referencePeriod: Podes 2024: one year preceding May 2024 enumeration (not calendar 2023)
updateFrequency: Podes major census three times per decade; this publication reports the 2024 round. Publication catalogue also labels release frequency annual; do not infer annual comparable theft observations.
missingness: All 27 selected theft-column cells are published numeric counts; no selected cell is blank or a missing-value symbol. No filling, imputation or forced zero occurs. Presence of a published count does not establish complete detection of underlying crime.
geographicLevel: Civil kabupaten/kota aggregation of desa/kelurahan occurrence reports
definition: Number of desa/kelurahan in each civil kabupaten/kota where theft (Pencurian, Table 18.4 column 2) occurred during the year before enumeration. This counts village-level presence, not police reports, incidents, victims or residents. Robbery (Pencurian dengan Kekerasan) is a separate column and is not added.
numerator: Source-published count of desa/kelurahan reporting theft occurrence in the preceding year.
denominator: None: absolute village/kelurahan count. No population or village-share rate is constructed.
measurementMethod: Podes 2024 civil administrative census, enumerated May 2024. Trained BPS personnel/partners directly interviewed relevant knowledgeable, authorized local informants and examined related documents. General explanations paragraph 6 explicitly assigns Table 18.4 to the preceding-year reference period. BPS publishes the kabupaten/kota aggregation; no police jurisdiction crosswalk is used.
licenseOrUsageNotes: Current BPS website section 13 explicitly permits commercial/noncommercial statistical-data use, copying/distribution and extraction with BPS credit, content title, access date, direct original link, lawful use and no false endorsement. PDF page 4 separately prohibits partial/full commercial book reproduction without written permission. Audit relies only on the explicit current statistical-data extraction grant for narrowly attributed factual cells; it does not redistribute the PDF, layout, images or full table text. Conflicting publication notice remains a downstream commercial-reuse review caveat; no open licence is fabricated.

comparability.reason: All 27 civil-region counts use one BPS Podes census, one selected category and one recall period; civil administrative scope is explicit in method. Raw village counts vary with numbers and sizes of villages, local recall and detection, so this audit disables cross-region ranking and risk comparisons.

temporalWarning: Collected in May 2024; Table 18.4 refers to the preceding year. Do not relabel this recall window as calendar 2023 or align it mechanically with 2023 CORE values.
limitations: Nearby-year context, not an actual calendar-2023 police-crime measure.
Method states one year before May 2024 enumeration but does not supply exact day-level start/end dates; no artificial calendar boundaries are imposed.
Only theft column is transcribed; no all-crime total is obtained by adding overlapping crime categories.
Canonical IDs are assigned from explicit civil BPS administrative scope and unambiguous regency/city labels; source table supplies names, not machine-readable region codes.
No denominator rate, population-risk estimate, ranking, danger classification, resident-stress inference or CORE integration is supported.
Current website extraction grant and older PDF commercial reproduction notice must both remain visible in downstream rights review.
knownBiases: Local-informant awareness, recall, record access and willingness to disclose affect reported occurrence.
Unreported or undetected theft can be missed; occurrence is not police-recorded incidence.
One village with one incident and one village with many incidents each contribute one to the published count.
Regions differ in village/kelurahan counts, village population and geographic size; raw counts are not a risk rate.
safeStatements: In Podes 2024, BPS recorded desa/kelurahan with theft occurrence during the year preceding May 2024 enumeration.
These values count villages/kelurahan with occurrence, not theft incidents or affected people.
unsafeStatements: These are calendar-year 2023 police-recorded crime counts.
This number is the count of theft incidents or victims.
Higher counts mean residents are more unsafe or stressed.
This is the percentage or probability of residents experiencing crime.
Adding the crime-type village counts gives distinct villages with any crime.
statementTemplates: BPS Podes 2024 recorded {value} desa/kelurahan in {regionName} with theft occurrence during the year preceding May 2024 enumeration; this is not an incident count or resident-risk rate.

sources.publisher: Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Jawa Barat
sources.title: Statistik Potensi Desa Provinsi Jawa Barat 2024, Table 18.4
sources.representation: Researcher-authored audit receipt with attributed metadata/short excerpts
sources.evidence: Publication 32000.24074 released 27 December 2024. PDF Table 18.4 printed page 187 / PDF page 215 contains column (2), Pencurian, for all 27 explicitly civil Kabupaten/Kota rows; continuation printed page 188 is not needed for the selected theft column. Civil administrative census scope is confirmed in general explanations, not inferred from table title alone. Only column (2) factual values are transcribed into observations; no full table/page text or layout is retained. Source labels distinguish plain regency names from Kota names, exactly matching canonical CIVX civil regions after adding the Kabupaten type label.

sources.retrievalMethod: Followed current public publication-page download link in memory; pdftotext extraction of relevant PDF definitions and selected numeric column. Hash covers actual PDF bytes; no PDF file, image, signed download URL or complete table retained.

sources.publisher: Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Jawa Barat
sources.title: Statistik Potensi Desa Provinsi Jawa Barat 2024, general explanations and security technical notes
sources.representation: Researcher-authored audit receipt with attributed metadata/short excerpts
sources.evidence: Executive summary printed vii / PDF 9 dates the census to May 2024. General explanations printed xxiv–xxv / PDF 26–27 establish civil census scope, definitive operational administrative areas with clear boundaries, and direct interviews by trained BPS staff/partners with knowledgeable responsible local informants plus related documents. Paragraph 6 explicitly lists Table 18.4 among tables referring to one year before enumeration; therefore this is preceding-year recall at May 2024, not calendar-year 2023. Chapter 18 technical notes printed 183 / PDF 211 define crime broadly, including attempts; selected column is theft and excludes the separately listed robbery column. These are village occurrence indicators, not numbers of incidents, police reports, victims or exposed residents.
sources.retrievalMethod: Inspected PDF pages 9, 26–28 and 211 through in-memory text extraction. Only narrow attributed method excerpts retained.
